newsitem.title: USA: Expert at Simpson trial says gloves didn't shrink.
newsitem.headline: Expert at Simpson trial says gloves didn't shrink.

text.p: A forensic scientist testified at O.J. Simpson's civil trial Monday that his experiments showed leather gloves similar to bloody ones found at the murder scene and Simpson's estate did not shrink when soaked in blood.

The testimony, which was not heard at last year's murder trial, supported the defence theory expressed to the jury at the criminal trial by attorney Johnnie Cochran that if "they (the gloves) don't fit, you must acquit."

Simpson had dramatically tried on the bloody gloves during the criminal trial and they apparently did not fit. He was subsequently found not guilty of murdering his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman.
The prosecution contended the gloves belonged to the ex-football star and were worn by the killer. They shrank after being soaked in blood, the criminal prosecutors argued.

But at the civil trial Monday, where Simpson is being sued for "wrongful death," forensic expert Herbert MacDonell said he carried out an experiment on Aris Isotoner Light leather gloves similar to those found at the murder scene and at Simpson's estate.

"I did not detect any measurable shrinkage in either glove," MacDonell told defence attorney Robert Baker. He said he had soaked the two XL-size gloves with 2mm each of his own blood and allowed it to soak into the gloves in an experiment at his laboratory. He then dried them on a copying machine and measured them again to see if they had shrunk.

MacDonell, who is one of the world's top experts on bloodstains, also repeated his testimony at the criminal trial that a pattern of stains on a sock at Simpson's home indicated the blood may have been planted, as the defence contends.
